body:
Source: GitHub issue #994 (bug, area:autopilot). Re-verified on main @ c410918c.

THE DEFECT. `packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs:265-267` inside `ac9_wallClockKillsFleet`:

    let spins = 0;
    while (fx.state.fleetRuns === 0 && spins++ < 50_000) await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));
    assert.equal(fx.state.fleetRuns, 1, 'fleet was dispatched and is hanging');

This is a busy-wait on a counter with an arbitrary iteration cap, not an await on the thing being waited for. Nothing ties the budget to the work: if the dispatch needs more than 50,000 `setImmediate` turns — or is waiting on I/O that a `setImmediate` spin does not advance — the loop exhausts and the assertion reports `expected 1, actual 0`. The failure message compounds it: 'fleet was dispatched and is hanging' describes the INTENDED state, so a reader concludes the hang under test occurred when in fact the dispatch never happened. A second instance of the same pattern is at `packages/autopilot/test/quota.test.mjs:216`: `let spins = 0; while (snapshot === null && spins++ < 50_000) await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r));`.

OBSERVED — three failures in one day (2026-09-11), all on diffs touching zero autopilot files: PR #989 `test (18)` run 34537547942 (AC9 direct, `expected 1, actual 0`); PR #991 `test (20)` run 34604456311 (AC9 direct); PR #991 `test (22)` same run (AC114 cascade — `AC114: every registered function is EXECUTED here…` failing with `AC9: ac9_wallClockKillsFleet failed without a fixture: fleet was dispatched and is hanging`). #991 was a documentation-only change. Each passed on re-run, and other node versions in the same run passed — the signature of a load-dependent timing budget, not a defect in the code under test. Re-running until green is what kept this invisible.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/autopilot` (the local issue autopilot). Run its suite with `npm test -w packages/autopilot` from the worktree root; a single file with `node --test packages/autopilot/test/<f>.test.mjs`. Module map for the files that matter here: `lib/run.mjs` (continueRun/resumeRun — the per-issue state machine), `lib/records.mjs` (the run-record store; `update` THROWS on a missing record), `lib/deps.mjs` (cloneAt/buildWorkerDeps/installGateDeps), `lib/paths.mjs` (the run directory layout incl. `gateDeps`), `lib/mirror.mjs` (worker + gate mirrors), `lib/git-env.mjs` (gitBaseEnv / NET_GIT template — carries the #962 gc.auto precedent), `test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs` and `test/helpers/sequence-fixture.mjs` (the two fixtures).

TEST-REGISTRY FACT you need before writing tests: `packages/autopilot/test/ac-registry.mjs` maps SPEC criterion numbers to test functions and `test/spec-coverage.test.mjs` enforces it. A regression test for a BUGFIX is NOT a spec criterion and MUST NOT be added to that registry — the precedent is the #962 fix (commit ca7299e5 / 763bd2a5), whose `ac962_…` tests are named after the ISSUE number and appear nowhere in `ac-registry.mjs`. Do not edit `ac-registry.mjs`, `test/spec-coverage.test.mjs`, or `docs/specs/issue-autopilot-local.md`.

The relevant fixture: `packages/autopilot/test/helpers/sequence-fixture.mjs` — `state` is declared at line 48 (`{ fleetRuns: 0, gateCalls: 0, reviewCalls: 0, checkPolls: 0, … }`) and `state.fleetRuns++` happens at line 127. That increment is the causal event AC9 is waiting for.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. THE WAIT BECOMES CAUSAL. The fixture must expose a way to await the dispatch — a deferred/promise resolved at the `state.fleetRuns++` site — and AC9 must await THAT. No iteration counter, no `setImmediate` spin, no polling interval standing in for the event. Put the helper on the fixture next to the state it observes, and make it usable for a dispatch that has ALREADY happened before the caller awaits (an await after the fact must resolve immediately, not hang) — a naive "create the promise on demand" helper silently reintroduces a race.
2. A BOUNDED FALLBACK MAY REMAIN ONLY AS A TIMEOUT, AND MUST BE HONEST. If the await carries a timeout so a genuinely broken dispatch fails the test rather than hanging the runner, the timeout path must report "the fleet dispatch never happened" — distinct from the assertion that the dispatch DID happen and hung. Those are different failures and only the second is what AC9 exists to test. The current single message conflating them is part of the defect, not incidental.
3. FIX BOTH INSTANCES. `quota.test.mjs:216` has the identical shape and the identical load-dependence; it gets the same treatment, against whatever its own causal event is (the `snapshot` assignment). Do not leave it "for later".
4. TEST-ONLY. No production `packages/autopilot/lib/**` file changes — this is a defect in how the tests wait, not in what they test. `lib/spawn.mjs` and `lib/quota.mjs` are rails. AC9 must keep asserting everything it asserts today: the deadline armed at 90 min + the 5-minute grace, `result.reason === 'wall-clock'`, `result.state === 'blocked'`, `fleetSpawn.result.timedOut === true`, and the `adlc:autopilot-blocked` label. The injected fake-timer table stays.
5. DO NOT REGISTER ANYTHING NEW IN `ac-registry.mjs`. AC9 and the quota ACs keep their existing registry entries, titles and exported function names — `spec-coverage.test.mjs` checks each registered test’s title and exported name, so renaming `ac9_wallClockKillsFleet` or changing its `AC9:` title breaks the coverage gate.
4. Documentation: NONE. This change alters no user-facing CLI surface, flag, exit code or output, so `packages/autopilot/README.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/autopilot.mdx` are NOT to be edited. (`docs/tools/autopilot.md` does not exist for this package.) Explain the change in the PR body instead.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 No bounded spin-wait remains anywhere in the autopilot test tree. verify: `grep -rn "spins++" packages/autopilot/ | wc -l` prints `0`
- AC2 The fixture’s dispatch signal resolves when the dispatch occurs AFTER the await begins, and ALSO resolves immediately when the dispatch already occurred BEFORE the await begins. Both directions asserted. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/sequence-fixture-signal.test.mjs`
- AC3 A dispatch that never happens produces a failure that says the dispatch never happened, textually distinct from the "dispatched and is hanging" assertion. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/sequence-fixture-signal.test.mjs`
- AC4 AC9 passes and still asserts all five of its original properties (deadline armed at 90min+5min grace, reason wall-clock, state blocked, the fleet child timedOut, the blocked label). verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs`
- AC5 AC9 is demonstrably not load-dependent: it passes with the event loop under contention. State in the PR body how you established this (e.g. the run under a background CPU load, or repeated runs) and what you observed. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/run.test.mjs` run repeatedly under load
- AC6 `quota.test.mjs` waits on its own causal event with no iteration counter, and its ACs still pass. verify: `node --test packages/autopilot/test/quota.test.mjs`
- AC7 Production code is untouched. verify: `git diff --stat origin/main -- packages/autopilot/lib/` prints nothing
- AC8 Existing suite green, including the coverage gate’s static checks. verify: `npm test -w packages/autopilot`
- AC10 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: issue #990 (the nested gate-deps gc guard) and issue #992 (the unguarded `records.update` in `continueRun`) are being fixed in two sibling branches at the same time. Do not touch `packages/autopilot/lib/run.mjs`, `packages/autopilot/test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs` or `packages/autopilot/test/loop.test.mjs` — edits there will collide. Also out of scope: issue #324, and any broader rework of the sequence fixture beyond the signal these ACs require.
title: autopilot: wait for the fleet dispatch on a causal signal instead of a bounded spin, and say which failure actually happened
